calibration.purpose: prove this oracle is the SAME implementation validated byte-exact against the live compiled runtime in live-runtime-diagnostic-parity-v1 (unmodified fixture_accepted/render_report/contains_banned_claim), AND that the identical banned phrase IS caught when written on a single narrative line rather than split across two -- isolating the cross-line mechanism as the sole cause of the bypass, not a general lint failure

claim_under_attack: amphora-report-packager/evidence/audit/live-runtime-diagnostic-parity-v1/live-runtime-diagnostic-parity-receipt.v1.dsse.json :: g1_outcome_labels ('real NFKC fullwidth banned-claim rejection') AND amphora-report-packager/evidence/audit/banned-claim-lint-parity-v1 (banned-claim lint genuinely polices overclaim content via normalize_claim/contains_banned_claim) AND docs/mission.md red-team dossier clause 'regulatory, supplier, procurement, qualification, or release overclaim. Every such case must fail closed or remain an explicit evidence gap.'
does_not_close: Does not promote the module, flip scientific_readiness, run the Rust runtime, supply real trust-anchored score envelopes, edit the master portfolio manifest, or perform the human dual-identity ceremony. Models the packaging-acceptance predicate from source bytes; the finding is a structural proof about the predicate as it exists in the current tree, not a legal/regulatory adjudication. Does not certify signed_report_package_present=true (hardcoded false pending Phase-1) or claim the production banned_claim_lint_pass gate (also hardcoded false, not wired to report_fixture_accepted) is affected.
mechanism: report_fixture_accepted's C10_narrative_lint clause is `fixture.payload.narrative.iter().any(|line| contains_banned_claim(line))` -- contains_banned_claim runs PER ARRAY ELEMENT, independently, never over the joined or rendered text. render_report() concatenates every narrative element in order, each terminated by a single newline, directly into the rendered document body -- there is no paragraph separator, sentinel, or re-scan step between elements. An adversary can therefore write any banned two-word phrase by ending one narrative array element with the phrase's first word and beginning the NEXT element with its second word: each element's normalized text lacks the full phrase, so contains_banned_claim returns false on both, and the `.any()` over the whole vector is false -- yet render_report emits them as two immediately adjacent lines that read, to a human viewing the rendered document, as one continuous overclaiming sentence. Unlike the zerowidth-lint-evasion-v1 vector (an invisible Unicode character inserted mid-token, defeating the alphanumeric sweep inside ONE line), this attack uses zero Unicode tricks -- every character is plain, visible ASCII -- and the defeated mechanism is per-element iteration versus whole-document scanning, not character normalization. Unlike title-overclaim-v1 (a field the lint never inspects at all), every character of this attack lives inside payload.narrative, the one field C10_narrative_lint actually runs over.
